title: Drop #8: Apr 5 to 11, 2026
intro: One week, boiled down. A shaky Iran ceasefire, an AI model that spooked the banks, Meta's new superintelligence play, Amazon's $200 billion AI bet, and two new college basketball champions.

spotlight.label: Organizations given Claude Mythos
spotlight.detail: Anthropic says the cyber-capable model is too powerful for a full public release.

note: Seven issues in this drop, plus a full podcast episode with Andrew and Ryan.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 5
issues.top: The business of pretending to be someone else

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: the money behind faux Elvises, Ben Franklins, and Disney princesses. Kept bite-sized.
Celebrity lookalikes are a real business
bullets.t: Top impersonators can earn up to $129,000 a year. A-list lookalikes get $500 to $10,000 per corporate gig; Pink Floyd tribute Brit Floyd asks $35,000 to $50,000. Estates push back: Johnny Cash's estate sued Coca-Cola under Tennessee's Elvis Act.

bullets.h: Princess parties and the 250th
bullets.t: Hired princesses boomed after the pandemic; one Indiana company charges $250 an hour and dodges Disney with names like Tower Princess. A full-time Ben Franklin gets 5 to 10 inquiries a day and charges $1,776 per keynote.

bullets.h: Quick hits
bullets.t: China has replica landmarks from the Colosseum to the Eiffel Tower. On Cameo, the most impersonated figure is Donald Trump (avg $78), then Elvis, Spider-Man, Jack Sparrow, and Lady Gaga.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 6
issues.top: US plastics makers win as Hormuz stays shut

bullets.h: The Malcolm in the Middle reboot is here, but Dewey turned down buckets of money to keep studying Dickens.
US plastics makers soar
bullets.t: With the Strait of Hormuz all but closed, US chemical firms using cheap natural gas are running flat out. Dow raised polyethylene prices 30 cents a pound; LyondellBasell stock is up 84% this year. Toy and packaging makers feel the squeeze.

bullets.h: UCLA women win first NCAA title
bullets.t: Beat South Carolina 79 to 51. First title for coach Cori Close, a longtime John Wooden mentee.

bullets.h: Women's sports money keeps climbing
bullets.t: Team investments up ~227% a year since 2022, per McKinsey. Revenue could hit ~$2.5 billion by 2030, growing about triple the rate of men's sports, but still under 2% of the US market. A record 63,000 fans saw an NWSL game; the PWHL sold out Madison Square Garden.

bullets.h: Daring rescue of downed airman
bullets.t: The missing F-15E weapons officer climbed a 7,000-foot ridge and hid in a crevice before a SEAL Team 6-led rescue with 100 special operators.

bullets.h: 44 years
bullets.t: The median US home is a record 44 years old. Structural repair costs rose ~14% in real terms from 2022 to 2024.

bullets.h: Writers Guild reaches tentative deal
bullets.t: About a month before the current contract expires.

bullets.h: scoff
bullets.t: To treat with derision.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 7
issues.top: OpenAI's playbook for a superintelligence economy

bullets.h: A Sunday special on investing is in the works. Pitch: your investing philosophy in one sentence.
OpenAI's superintelligence policy blueprint
bullets.t: Ideas include incentives for a four-day workweek, lower taxes on workers with AI-boom companies funding Social Security and SNAP, and a public wealth fund like Alaska's oil fund. Also more government help managing AI risks.

bullets.h: Claude Code pricing shift
bullets.t: Anthropic plans to charge extra to use OpenClaw and other third-party tools.

bullets.h: Michigan wins the men's title
bullets.t: Beat UConn 69 to 63. First title since 1989 and UConn's first-ever title game loss.

bullets.h: Angel Reese traded to Atlanta
bullets.t: The Sky get two first-round picks.

bullets.h: Brands flee a festival over Ye
bullets.t: Pepsi, Diageo, AB InBev, Rockstar, and PayPal pulled back from London's Wireless Festival after Ye was named headliner.

bullets.h: Phone-free dining spreads
bullets.t: Bars and restaurants in at least 11 states restrict phones. Some Chick-fil-A spots offer free ice cream to hand yours over.

bullets.h: Dimon's warning
bullets.t: JPMorgan's CEO called creeping inflation a possible skunk at the party.

bullets.h: moratorium
bullets.t: A temporary prohibition of an activity.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 8
issues.top: Data center backlash escalates; two-week ceasefire

bullets.h: Unhappy with the NBA dunk contest, Shaq is launching his own pro dunk league.
The fight over data centers turns ugly
bullets.t: Shots were fired at an Indianapolis councilor's home after he backed a data center; a note read No Data Centers. Maine is set to pause centers over 20 megawatts, nine states weigh statewide bans, and South Dakota and Wisconsin rejected them.

bullets.h: Medvi: billion-dollar startup, red flags
bullets.t: The AI-run GLP-1 telehealth firm expects $1.8 billion in sales with 2 employees. Reports flag fake before-and-after photos, AI testimonials, spam suits, and an FDA warning letter.

bullets.h: Anthropic's powerful new model
bullets.t: Apple, Amazon, and Microsoft get early access to prep for cyberattacks.

bullets.h: Google AI Overviews: ~90% accurate
bullets.t: Sounds good, but that's tens of millions of wrong answers an hour. Over half of accurate answers cited sources that didn't support them; Facebook and Reddit ranked second and fourth.

bullets.h: Two-week Iran ceasefire
bullets.t: Brokered by Pakistan, tied to reopening the Strait of Hormuz, about 90 minutes before Trump's deadline.

bullets.h: Ackman bids for Universal Music
bullets.t: Pershing Square offers about $64.4 billion.

bullets.h: Upper middle class is now the biggest group
bullets.t: 31% of families in 2024 vs 10% in 1979, per AEI. Near-poverty share fell below 19%.

bullets.h: rudimentary
bullets.t: Limited to basic principles; of a primitive kind.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 9
issues.top: Relief rally, shaky truce, Meta's new AI

bullets.h: RIP Jim Whittaker, REI's first full-time employee and the first American to summit Everest, at 97.
Meta launches Muse Spark
bullets.t: First model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, led by Alexandr Wang. Internal benchmarks beat Grok on most metrics and Gemini on some, competitive with OpenAI and Anthropic.

bullets.h: NYT names a Satoshi suspect
bullets.t: It pointed to British cryptographer Adam Back, narrowing 34,000 suspects to one. Back says they have the wrong guy. Satoshi's wallet holds an estimated $78 billion.

bullets.h: Ceasefire wobbles
bullets.t: Oil fell well below $100 on the truce, but Israeli strikes on Lebanon and doubts about Hormuz reopening made it look brittle.

bullets.h: Fed in wait-and-see mode
bullets.t: March minutes still point to one rate cut this year.

bullets.h: Levi's gets its groove back
bullets.t: Revenue up 14%; direct-to-consumer topped half of sales for the first time. Sales of the 517 jean jumped 25% after the Love Story series.

bullets.h: A 7-foot statue for a hero rat
bullets.t: Magawa sniffed out 100 land mines and cleared 1.52 million square feet in Cambodia. Now he has a monument.

bullets.h: perdurable
bullets.t: Very durable.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 10
issues.top: Iran war's lasting costs; Amazon goes all in on AI

bullets.h: Iced coffee season is officially open.
The war's long tail
bullets.t: Iran is charging some ships $2 million to transit Hormuz; traffic is under 10% of prewar. Oil may stay elevated through year end, fertilizer prices are rising, and the IMF will trim its 3.3% global growth forecast.

bullets.h: Amazon: not a hunch
bullets.t: Jassy defends roughly $200 billion in 2026 capex on AI, chips, robotics, and satellites, expecting payback starting next year.

bullets.h: Gen Z sours on AI
bullets.t: Gallup: angry rose from 22% to 31%; excited fell from 36% to 22%; hopeful from 27% to 18%.

bullets.h: DeChambeau's 3D-printed iron
bullets.t: The Scientist got USGA approval for a self-designed 5-iron at the Masters, then triple bogeyed the 11th in Round 1.

bullets.h: DOJ probes NFL TV deals
bullets.t: Looking at whether the league's rights maze hurts fans.

bullets.h: Disney plans up to 1,000 layoffs
bullets.t: New CEO Josh D'Amaro's first big move, mostly marketing.

bullets.h: US fertility rate hits a record low
bullets.t: Down ~1% last year and nearly 20% in two decades.

bullets.h: spurious
bullets.t: False, inauthentic, or contrived.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 11
issues.top: Anthropic's Mythos spooks the banks

bullets.h: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce save-the-dates are out, reportedly for NYC over July 4th. A Ben Franklin reenactor to officiate, please.
Claude Mythos alarms Washington
bullets.t: Powell and Bessent met bank CEOs after Anthropic's limited release to ~40 organizations. Humans find ~100 critical flaws a year; Mythos can find thousands. Short term edge to attackers, then defenders.

bullets.h: Inflation jumps to 3.3%
bullets.t: Highest in two years, driven by gas. Core rose just 0.2%.

bullets.h: Peace talks in Pakistan
bullets.t: JD Vance leads the US team; Iran set preconditions.

bullets.h: Businesses aren't fleeing NYC
bullets.t: Office vacancy fell to 13.5% as AI firms leased up, per JLL, despite tax fears under Mayor Mamdani.

bullets.h: A human-only Slack channel
bullets.t: An AI startup's 20 real employees hide from their AI coworkers.

bullets.h: Hedgehog-friendly lawns
bullets.t: German mayors want nighttime bans on robot mowers.

bullets.h: Michael J. Fox is fine
bullets.t: CNN apologized for an erroneous memorial piece.

bullets.h: Gas station speakeasy
bullets.t: Lakeville, Minnesota's hottest bar is behind a gas station.

bullets.h: deft
bullets.t: Characterized by facility and skill.

title: Drop #7: Mar 29 to Apr 4, 2026
intro: One week, boiled down. Gas crossed four dollars, SpaceX filed for a record IPO, Lilly got a GLP-1 pill approved, Italy missed another World Cup, and summer travel got a lot more expensive.

spotlight.label: SpaceX IPO raise target
spotlight.detail: At a $1.75 trillion valuation, per Bloomberg. Would smash the all-time IPO record.

note: Seven issues in this drop, plus a full podcast episode with Andrew and Ryan.

issues.label: Issue of Mar 29
issues.top: Event travel is the new boom town

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: sports, music, and pilgrimages powering local economies, plus Charted Territory and News You Can Use.
Music and sports tourism boom
bullets.t: Music tourism could top $9 billion by 2030. Sports tourism could pass $1 trillion. California hosts World Cup games, another Super Bowl, and the 2028 Olympics.

bullets.h: F1 keeps packing tracks
bullets.t: $3.9 billion in revenue last year, up 14%. 2025 drew 6.7 million fans; 19 events sold out. Two Middle East races canceled, ~$200 million hit.

bullets.h: Quick hits
bullets.t: Sturgis Motorcycle Rally draws ~500,000 to a town of 7,000. Religious tourism was nearly $290 billion in 2024, from Hajj to Kumbh Mela.

bullets.h: A yearlong US holiday road trip, mapped
bullets.t: Possum Drop in Tallapoosa, Mardi Gras, Loveland Sweetheart Festival, Reno's leprechaun crawl, Tulsa Juneteenth, Mount Rushmore July 4, then Leavenworth Oktoberfest, Anoka Halloween capital, Branson Veterans Day, Chicago Turkey Trot, and North Pole, New York.

bullets.h: 2026 events worth the trip
bullets.t: San Marcos Fair (Apr-May), World Cup across US/Canada/Mexico (Jun-Jul, US vs Paraguay Jun 12 in LA), Edinburgh Fringe (Aug), Munich Oktoberfest (Sep-Oct), Thailand lantern festivals (Nov 24-25), Sydney New Year's Eve.

issues.label: Issue of Mar 30
issues.top: Iran war hits aluminum, Lilly bets on AI drugs

bullets.h: A truck with 400,000 KitKats was stolen in Italy. Supply is fine: they were Formula 1 KitKats.
Iran hits Gulf aluminum plants
bullets.t: Attacks damaged Emirates Global Aluminium and Alba. Middle East makes ~9% of global aluminum; prices up ~4% since the war began.

bullets.h: Eli Lilly's $2.75B AI drug deal
bullets.t: Deal with Insilico Medicine; $115 million up front. Lilly gets exclusive rights to an Insilico GLP-1 for diabetes.

bullets.h: Houthis enter the Iran war
bullets.t: Yemen's Houthis launched missiles at Israel. 2,500 Marines arrived in the region aboard the USS Tripoli.

bullets.h: US lets a Russian oil tanker reach Cuba
bullets.t: Trump said Cuba has to survive.

bullets.h: Zillow Preview spreads
bullets.t: 29 brokerages now show pre-listings; rivals launched their own.

bullets.h: Chesney the kangaroo, 3 days on the hop
bullets.t: Escaped a Wisconsin farm after dogs spooked him. Keeper walked ~37,000 steps a day; a drone found him unharmed.

bullets.h: Project Hail Mary stays No. 1
bullets.t: Biggest Hollywood flick of the year so far.

bullets.h: apparatus
bullets.t: Material or equipment designed for a specific use.

issues.label: Issue of Mar 31
issues.top: Private assets may enter your 401(k)

bullets.h: Happy 99th to William Daniels, aka Mr. Feeny.
Riskier options headed for 401(k)s
bullets.t: Proposed rule would shield employers who add private assets. Critics note private credit turmoil and weaker recent returns.

bullets.h: Trump threatens Iran energy sites
bullets.t: Unless Hormuz reopens soon, including electricity, oil wells, and Kharg Island.

bullets.h: Powell: oil shock likely won't force hikes
bullets.t: Fed chair said energy shocks are usually short-lived.

bullets.h: Sysco to buy Jetro for $29 billion
bullets.t: Restaurant Depot's 166-store cash-and-carry chain.

bullets.h: $10 million art heist in under 3 minutes
bullets.t: Thieves took a Renoir, a Cézanne, and a Matisse from a museum outside Parma.

bullets.h: Women's Final Four set
bullets.t: UConn, UCLA, Texas, and South Carolina, same four as last year.

bullets.h: accolade
bullets.t: An award or privilege granted as a special honor.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 1
issues.top: US gas hits $4 a gallon

bullets.h: April Fools'. Also, Apple turns 50.
Gas averages $4.02 a gallon
bullets.t: First time above $4 since 2022; up 35% since the war began. California hit $5.91. Strategic reserves, looser fuel rules, and driver rebates are in play.

bullets.h: Allbirds sells for $39 million
bullets.t: Once valued at $4 billion on IPO day. Keeps two outlets; Ed Hardy owner buys the assets.

bullets.h: McCormick buys Unilever foods for $45 billion
bullets.t: Hellmann's and Knorr are ~70% of that food sales.

bullets.h: Whoop hits a $10 billion valuation
bullets.t: Raised $575 million; bookings up 103% last year.

bullets.h: Apple at 50
bullets.t: $3.7 trillion market cap, 2.5 billion active devices, 166,000 employees.

bullets.h: Oracle starts AI-driven layoffs
bullets.t: Thousands cut as it spends billions on data centers. CoreWeave jumped on a big AI infrastructure loan.

bullets.h: nullified
bullets.t: Made legally null and void; invalidated.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 2
issues.top: SpaceX files for the biggest IPO ever

bullets.h: April 2: you can believe the internet again.
SpaceX targets a $75 billion IPO
bullets.t: At a $1.75 trillion valuation, per Bloomberg. Would top Saudi Aramco's $29 billion record. Up to 30% of shares may go to retail. xAI rides along.

bullets.h: Nike's China slump deepens
bullets.t: Seventh straight quarterly sales drop there. Shares fell ~15% despite a North America bounce.

bullets.h: Lilly's Foundayo GLP-1 pill approved
bullets.t: Second oral option after Wegovy. Analysts see ~$21 billion by 2030 vs $4 billion for Wegovy pill. Lilly has ~$1.5 billion of pills ready.

bullets.h: Is grad school worth it?
bullets.t: AU study: pharmacy +68%, medicine +173%, law +41%, MBA +13%, clinical psych -5%.

bullets.h: Anthropic leaks Claude Code source
bullets.t: Accidental leak of internal source for the popular coding tool.

bullets.h: Megan Thee Stallion back to Broadway
bullets.t: Returns to Moulin Rouge after a mid-show hospitalization.

bullets.h: pedagogy
bullets.t: The method and practice of teaching.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 3
issues.top: Summer travel gets expensive; Tesla misses

bullets.h: A quarter of 2026 is already gone.
Summer trips look pricey
bullets.t: Global airfares up 24% YoY. Transatlantic tickets +$200 in a month. United cuts ~5% of off-peak flights. Only 17% of Americans plan international trips.

bullets.h: Tesla's soft quarter
bullets.t: 358k deliveries, undershot forecasts. Stock fell ~6% that day, ~20% YTD. Gas spike may help rivals' EVs.

bullets.h: Italy misses a third straight World Cup
bullets.t: Fell to Bosnia. Federation brass resign. First World Cup winner to miss three in a row.

bullets.h: OpenAI buys tech talk show TBPN
bullets.t: First media foray.

bullets.h: Maine moves to ban new data centers
bullets.t: Would be the first state, per the Journal.

bullets.h: Blue Owl caps private credit redemptions
bullets.t: Latest firm to limit cashouts amid software-loan fears.

bullets.h: $1,200 barista bonuses
bullets.t: Starbucks: up to $300 a quarter if stores hit goals; pay up 5% to 8%.

bullets.h: procure
bullets.t: To obtain something with care or effort.

issues.label: Issue of Apr 4
issues.top: Jobs rebound; a $2.2T budget ask

bullets.h: Tax Day is April 15. Cookie if you're done.
Trump seeks a $2.2 trillion budget
bullets.t: $1.5 trillion for defense (+42%). Cuts hit SBA, EPA, HHS, and NASA. Redirects $15 billion from clean energy toward fossil fuels and AI supercomputers.

bullets.h: US adds 178,000 jobs in March
bullets.t: Unemployment 4.3%. Healthcare led hiring.

bullets.h: Crew rescued after jet downed over Iran
bullets.t: One of two F-15E crew members recovered; a second US plane, an A-10, was also shot down.

bullets.h: Jonathan the tortoise is fine
bullets.t: Hoax death reports were wrong. He's 193.

bullets.h: Meta tests premium Instagram
bullets.t: Includes viewing stories without the poster knowing.

bullets.h: MLB robot umps shrink listed heights
bullets.t: League revised dozens of player heights for the strike zone.

bullets.h: Costco's 10-pound chocolate bunny
bullets.t: Pete the Bunny. Bring a hammer.

bullets.h: confection
bullets.t: A dish made with sweet ingredients.

title: Drop #6: Mar 22 to 28, 2026
intro: One week, boiled down. Meta and YouTube lost in court twice, senators went after sports prediction markets, the NBA eyed Seattle and Vegas, and tech stocks slid into a correction.

spotlight.label: People the US added in a year
spotlight.detail: One of the slowest growth rates in history.

note: Seven issues in this drop, plus a full podcast episode with Andrew and Ryan.

issues.label: Issue of Mar 22
issues.top: Touching grass: the business of meeting people IRL

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: logging off and socializing in person, from dinner clubs to friend pitch decks.
Dinner clubs woo dating app defectors
bullets.t: Dinner Table Club, TimeLeft and Thursday host in-person singles events; Hinge funds IRL dating grants.

bullets.h: Meetup tries a comeback
bullets.t: After WeWork and a sale to Bending Spoons, fees rose to $45 a month but new registrations grew 20%.

bullets.h: Quick hits
bullets.t: Pitch decks for single friends, solo travel in groups (70%+ women), and the run club debate.

issues.label: Issue of Mar 23
issues.top: Rising gas prices spark new interest in EVs

bullets.h: Happy Near Miss Day: 37 years since a half-mile-wide asteroid passed within 500,000 miles of Earth.
Gas prices push buyers toward EVs
bullets.t: The federal credit is gone, but dealer deals are steep: one buyer got a 2026 Equinox EV for $23,991, over 50% off sticker. Tesla plans 15,000 Semis by the end of 2026.

bullets.h: Walmart goes all digital on price tags
bullets.t: All US stores switch to digital shelf labels by year end. Walmart says no surge pricing; some lawmakers want paper tags required.

bullets.h: $200 million: Cargill's AI meat-fleck haul
bullets.t: AI scans carcasses for missed meat, recovering up to 0.5% more per animal across 11 billion pounds of beef a year.

bullets.h: Ovechkin hits 1,000 goals
bullets.t: Only Wayne Gretzky reached the mark before him.

bullets.h: MLB season opens this week
bullets.t: The Dodgers are favored to repeat.

bullets.h: Project Hail Mary opens big
bullets.t: $80.5 million, Amazon MGM's biggest opening ever.

bullets.h: Iran threatens to fully close Hormuz
bullets.t: If Trump follows through on threats to its power plants.

issues.label: Issue of Mar 24
issues.top: Senators move to ban sports prediction markets

bullets.h: MLB starts tomorrow night. Sunflower seed season is back.
Bipartisan bill targets sports prediction markets
bullets.t: It would bar Kalshi and Polymarket from sports and casino contracts. Kalshi did 90% of NFL-season volume on sports and $2.67 billion in sports trades in one March Madness week.

bullets.h: March Madness ratings up
bullets.t: Opening games drew 9.8 million viewers, up 6%.

bullets.h: Samsung fridge ads spark backlash
bullets.t: Banner ads on $1,800+ Family Hub fridges; turning them off also kills the news and weather widget.

bullets.h: Corporate BS fans are worse at their jobs
bullets.t: A Cornell study of 1,000+ workers found those most impressed by jargon scored lower on decision-making tests.

bullets.h: Larry Fink: AI could widen inequality
bullets.t: The BlackRock CEO urged people to invest in top AI companies.

bullets.h: DoorDash helps drivers with gas
bullets.t: Extra pay for US and Canadian drivers to offset fuel prices.

bullets.h: TotalEnergies drops US offshore wind
bullets.t: It will exit nearly $1 billion in leases and invest in US oil and gas instead.

issues.label: Issue of Mar 25
issues.top: Private credit funds limit withdrawals

bullets.h: Tolkien Reading Day, marking the day the One Ring was destroyed.
Private credit has a public freakout
bullets.t: Apollo and Ares capped payouts after investors asked to cash out over 11% of shares. Moody's cut a KKR-linked fund to junk.

bullets.h: Report: 3,000 troops of the 82nd Airborne to the Middle East
bullets.t: No decision on ground troops in Iran; Pakistan offered to mediate.

bullets.h: CERN moves antimatter by truck
bullets.t: A 30-minute test drive with 92 antiprotons, a first step toward an eight-hour trip to Germany.

bullets.h: Zoox expands robotaxis
bullets.t: Miami and Austin are next this year.

bullets.h: OpenAI shuts down Sora
bullets.t: Months after launch, as it refocuses on business and coding.

bullets.h: Reality TV is shrinking
bullets.t: Unscripted US premieres fell 15% last year and by a third since 2022.

bullets.h: Meta owes $375 million in New Mexico
bullets.t: A jury found it failed to protect young users from predators.

bullets.h: Apple Maps will show ads this summer

issues.label: Issue of Mar 26
issues.top: Meta and YouTube lose a landmark addiction trial

bullets.h: Stellantis is ticketing employees who park cars from other automakers in the company lot.
Social media's Big Tobacco moment?
bullets.t: A California jury found Meta and YouTube negligent in a bellwether addiction case; they owe $4.2 million and $1.8 million. Both will appeal. Section 230 did not shield them.

bullets.h: NBA heads to Seattle and Las Vegas
bullets.t: Owners voted to start vetting teams 31 and 32 for 2028-29, with fees of $7 to $10 billion each.

bullets.h: Fruit Love Island gets the boot
bullets.t: The AI fruit parody hit 3.3 million followers before TikTok removed it.

bullets.h: Postage up 8%
bullets.t: USPS cites rising fuel costs.

bullets.h: Labubu worries sink Pop Mart
Trump to visit Xi in May

issues.label: Issue of Mar 27
issues.top: US population growth slows to a historic low

bullets.h: Dodger Stadium is now Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium.
US adds just 1.8 million people
bullets.t: Lower immigration drove the slowdown. Miami-Dade flipped to a 10,000-person drop, while the Southeast and Texas suburbs boomed.

bullets.h: FCC halts approval of new foreign routers
bullets.t: Existing models stay legal. TP-Link plans US manufacturing; Netgear shares rose.

bullets.h: DraftKings lets you bet on old pitches
bullets.t: DK Replay uses anonymized historic at-bats, Oregon only for now.

bullets.h: IOC bars transgender women from female events
bullets.t: Citing a policy aligned with a recent executive order.

bullets.h: $26 million turned down
bullets.t: Kentucky farmers refused an AI company's data center offer, about 10x local land value.

bullets.h: OpenAI shelves erotic ChatGPT indefinitely
Netflix standard rises $2 to $19.99
bullets.t: Plus a Jeopardy! spinoff for YouTube is in the works.

issues.label: Issue of Mar 28
issues.top: Nasdaq slides into correction

bullets.h: Last weekend in March: stock up on allergy meds.
Tech drags the Nasdaq into correction
bullets.t: Down 11% from its October peak. Microsoft is off 34% and having its worst quarter since 2008; Meta down 29%; Nvidia nearly 20%.

bullets.h: Rough first week for Disney's new CEO
bullets.t: Josh D'Amaro faced a Bachelorette scandal, the end of a $1 billion Sora deal, and 1,000+ Epic Games layoffs.

bullets.h: Tiger Woods arrested on suspicion of DUI
bullets.t: After a rollover crash in Florida.

bullets.h: SAVE plan winds down
bullets.t: Seven million student loan borrowers must pick a new repayment option.

bullets.h: PS5 prices are going up

title: Drop #5: Mar 15 to 21, 2026

spotlight.label: New average WNBA salary
spotlight.detail: Up from about $120,000 under the new labor deal.

note: Seven issues in this drop, plus a full podcast episode with Andrew and Ryan.

issues.label: Issue of Mar 15
issues.top: The changing face of the beauty industry

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: the business of looking good, from makeup for minors to some truly wild cosmetic trends.
The beauty biz gets a makeover
bullets.t: Men are warming to makeup (75% say they never wear it, down from 90% in 2019), brands are selling glitter to kids as young as 5, and K-beauty sales in the US more than doubled since 2023.

bullets.h: AI deepfakes hit beauty influencers
bullets.t: Scammers use AI clones of real influencers and doctors to push products they never endorsed.

bullets.h: Celeb beauty brands mint moguls
bullets.t: Elf bought Hailey Bieber's Rhode for $1 billion, Rare Beauty is valued near $2.7 billion, and Rihanna's Fenty stake is worth about $700 million.

bullets.h: Hair transplant trips to Turkey
bullets.t: Grafts run $3,000 to $9,000 there versus up to $24,000 in the US, often bundled with a luxury hotel stay.

bullets.h: Wait, what? Cadaver fat injections
bullets.t: Some execs are filling out curves with purified donor fat, partly to counter the GLP-1 deflation effect.

issues.label: Issue of Mar 16
issues.top: One Battle After Another rules the Oscars

bullets.h: Bracket season is here. Your odds of a perfect one by coin flip: 1 in 9.2 quintillion.
Gas prices to stay high while Hormuz is unsafe
bullets.t: The energy secretary offered 'no guarantees in war,' and Trump urged NATO to send warships.

bullets.h: FCC chair threatens broadcast licenses
bullets.t: Brendan Carr accused outlets of 'news distortions' over Iran war coverage.

bullets.h: One Battle After Another wins six Oscars
bullets.t: Including best picture. Michael B. Jordan won best actor for Sinners, and KPop Demon Hunters took best animated feature.

bullets.h: Dick's Sporting Goods is on a winning streak
bullets.t: Sales roughly doubled in 10 years, riding a $40 billion youth sports market.

bullets.h: A dog dad used AI to fight his pup's cancer
bullets.t: With help from ChatGPT and AlphaFold, he got a custom mRNA shot made for Rosie, and her tumor shrank by half. Not a cure, and experts warn it won't generalize.

bullets.h: $40 trillion: what older women are set to inherit
bullets.t: Mostly by outliving their husbands, as part of the great wealth transfer.

The Supreme Court rules Trump's global tariffs illegal

bullets.t: Iran says it will send a proposed deal within days.

A sleeper shark was spotted swimming in the near-freezing waters of Antarctica
Sam Altman and Dario Amodei avoided holding hands at India's AI summit photo op
Shenanigans
bullets.t: Means 'high-spirited or mischievous activity.'

Is private equity past its prime?

bullets.t: Font library Monotype, big music catalogs, and YouTube channels like Cocomelon.

Companies face an uphill climb for tariff refunds

bullets.h: One Battle After Another wins best film at the BAFTAs

bullets.h: 10%: drop in AMC attendance last year

Jamie Dimon's 'anxiety is high'

bullets.h: Novo Nordisk slashes Ozempic and Wegovy prices

bullets.h: Dark Sky's creators launch Acme Weather

title: Drop #2: Feb 1 to 14, 2026
intro: Two more weeks, boiled down. Big Tech's AI spending plans topped $650 billion, bitcoin sank below $70,000, Disney picked a new CEO, and the Seahawks won Super Bowl LX.

spotlight.label: Super Bowls attended
spotlight.detail: Three lifelong fans have been to every single one, since 1967 when a ticket cost $12.

note: Fourteen issues in this drop, one for every day.

issues.label: Issue of Feb 1
issues.top: The business of sports fandom is changing

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: the business of sports fandom, from jerseys to stadium hot dogs.
Fanatics wants to be your whole fan life
bullets.t: The merch giant brought in about $13 billion last year and wants to hit $50 billion. Its betting arm doubled to about 8% market share, and a branded credit card arrives this spring.

bullets.h: That ticket might not be yours to sell
bullets.t: Teams use digital-only tickets, price floors, and fines to limit resale. The NFL fined more than 100 players and staff for flipping Super Bowl tickets last year.

bullets.h: Stadium food is getting cheaper
bullets.t: After Atlanta cut hot dogs from $8 to $2, transactions jumped 30%. Utah, Phoenix, and Baltimore followed, though one Commanders beer still cost $16.49.

bullets.h: Pop culture is minting new fans
bullets.t: Hockey ticket interest on StubHub spiked 40% during the hit show Heated Rivalry, and Taylor Swift tripled Chiefs home ticket sales on StubHub.

bullets.h: Free stuff fills seats
bullets.t: Bobbleheads, jerseys, and quirky giveaways keep stands full, especially in baseball. The Panthers once offered a lifetime supply of mayo for every forced turnover.

issues.top: AI agents get their own social network

bullets.h: It's Groundhog Day. Phil's overall forecast accuracy is about 35%, so we'll take the over.
Bitcoin slips below $76,000
bullets.t: That's about 40% off its October high, after a fourth straight losing month.

bullets.h: Shutdown fix in sight, maybe
bullets.t: House Speaker Mike Johnson says the partial shutdown will end by Tuesday, but the House margins are razor thin.

bullets.h: Kendrick Lamar and Bad Bunny sweep the Grammys

bullets.h: Walmart and Target get new CEOs
bullets.t: John Furner takes over a thriving Walmart, while Michael Fiddelke inherits a Target with 10 of the last 12 quarters flat or down.

bullets.h: Alcaraz wins the Australian Open
bullets.t: He beat Djokovic and became the youngest player to complete a career Grand Slam.

bullets.h: Moltbook mania: hilarity or singularity?
bullets.t: A Reddit-style site where only AI agents post claimed 1.5 million users and an AI religion called Crustafarianism. Musk called it the early stages of the singularity, while skeptics say many posts are fake.

bullets.h: 28: days of calendar perfection
bullets.t: February starts on a Sunday and ends on a Saturday, a perfect four-week grid. The last time was 2015, and the next is 2037.

bullets.h: Thaumaturgy
bullets.t: Means 'magic' or 'miracle-working.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 3
issues.top: Musk merges SpaceX and xAI

bullets.h: Phil saw his shadow, so it's six more weeks of winter, and the crowd booed him.
The US and India strike a trade deal
bullets.t: US tariffs on Indian goods drop to 18%, and India agrees to stop buying Russian oil.

bullets.h: Project Vault: a $12 billion minerals stockpile
bullets.t: The US is stashing rare earths and critical minerals, about 60 days' worth, to loosen China's grip on supply.

bullets.h: Disney's next CEO may come from the parks
bullets.t: Parks chief Josh D'Amaro is the favorite, helped by a record $10 billion quarterly profit from parks and cruises.

bullets.h: Crying horse replaces Labubu
bullets.t: A $3.60 plush horse with an upside-down snout went viral, and about 15,000 are ordered daily.

bullets.h: Musk merges SpaceX and xAI
bullets.t: The deal values the combined company at about $1.25 trillion, and Musk is pitching data centers in space.

bullets.h: 393,812: minivans sold last year, up 21%

bullets.h: Tchotchke
bullets.t: Means 'a knickknack.'

issues.top: PayPal's stock tanks as it replaces its CEO

PayPal swaps its CEO and the stock tanks

bullets.h: The House ends the partial shutdown
bullets.t: A $1.2 trillion funding bill passed, but Homeland Security is only funded through Feb. 13.

bullets.h: Disney taps parks boss Josh D'Amaro as CEO

bullets.t: Means 'the act of spreading something widely.'

The last US-Russia nuclear treaty expires

bullets.t: The EEOC is looking at whether its diversity goals led to unfair treatment of white employees.

bullets.h: The Washington Post lays off 30% of its staff
bullets.t: More than 300 of 800 journalists are cut, shrinking international coverage and nearly erasing the sports desk.

bullets.t: Means 'loud and clear.'

The Hollywood Reporter asked whether underwear is the new tequila
Emblazoned

bullets.t: Tyreek Hill said 'those state taxes, man,' and saved about $9 million by signing in Florida. Mikko Rantanen's Texas deal is worth about $4 million more.

bullets.h: A side hustle tax tip
bullets.t: Track every expense all year in a simple spreadsheet, match costs to tax categories, and hire a pro once you get more than two forms.

bullets.h: Famous tax troubles
bullets.t: Willie Nelson, Floyd Mayweather, and Al Capone all tangled with the taxman. Nelson even released an album to repay the IRS.

issues.top: Seahawks win Super Bowl LX

bullets.h: Jimmy Lai sentenced to 20 years

bullets.t: The operation led to more than 4,000 arrests, mass protests, and the deaths of two US citizens. A small team stays behind.

bullets.h: The DOJ antitrust chief resigns
bullets.t: Gail Slater was reportedly pushed out after months of clashes with leadership.

bullets.h: The EPA formally repeals its climate finding
bullets.t: Environmental groups plan to sue, and the Supreme Court may have the last word.

bullets.h: Hilary Duff announces her first world tour in nearly 20 years
Home sales fall 8.4%
bullets.t: Existing-home sales dropped in January, the worst month for closings in more than two years.

bullets.h: Olympic drones steal the show
bullets.t: More than two dozen drones film luge and skiing, but athletes and viewers are bothered by the whirring.

bullets.h: Apple may delay its Siri upgrades
bullets.t: Bloomberg says testing issues could push the planned changes back.

bullets.h: 22%: how much ground beef prices rose in two years
bullets.t: Boneless chicken prices fell 1.7%, so dark meat is in demand.

bullets.h: Volition
bullets.t: Means 'the power to make your own decisions.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 14
issues.top: Inflation is finally taking a chill pill

bullets.h: Happy Valentine's Day. Roses are red, violets are blue, and we love you, too.
Inflation cools to 2.4%
bullets.t: Prices rose 0.2% in January. Gas fell 3.2% and eggs dropped 7%, but airfare jumped 6.5%.

bullets.h: Homeland Security shuts down over the ICE fight
bullets.t: Funding lapsed as Democrats push for limits on ICE. TSA and Coast Guard staff could miss paychecks if it drags on.

bullets.h: Dubai port boss quits over Epstein ties
bullets.t: DP World's CEO resigned after emails with Epstein came out.

bullets.h: Quad God takes two falls
bullets.t: Ilia Malinin fell twice in his free skate and is out of medal contention.

bullets.h: Ring drops its Flock Safety partnership
bullets.t: The split follows backlash over its Super Bowl ad.

bullets.h: Hollywood vs. the fake Cruise and Pitt fight
bullets.t: A viral AI clip made with ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 drew copyright complaints from the film studios' trade group and SAG-AFTRA.

bullets.h: A Manhattan restaurant now lets diners bring an AI companion as a date
A Stanford student is using an algorithm to pair 5,000 singles
A Slovak fugitive was arrested at an Olympic hockey game
Nick Castellanos says he was benched for bringing a beer into the dugout
Deceleration
bullets.t: Means 'reduction in speed or rate.'

title: Drop #1: Jan 18 to 31, 2026
intro: Two weeks of headlines, boiled down. Greenland tariff threats whipsawed markets, gold blew past $5,000, TikTok went American and then got messy, and Trump named Kevin Warsh as the next Fed chair.

spotlight.label: Seconds to midnight
spotlight.detail: The Doomsday Clock has never been this close.

note: Twelve issues in this drop. Issues for Jan 25 and Jan 26 were not available.

issues.label: Issue of Jan 18
issues.top: Watches are having their finest hour

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: watches, from the White Rabbit's pocketwatch to James Bond's Omega.
Watches are in their finest hour
bullets.t: Gen Z is shopping secondhand and following watch influencers. The used-watch market hit $27 billion in 2023, and only a few models, like the Rolex Daytona and GMT, still trade at a big premium.

bullets.h: Trends that make your wrist stand out
bullets.t: Odd shapes (a padlock, a bathroom scale, a panther), retro vintage pieces, sustainable materials, and bold colors like avocado and candy pink.

bullets.h: Is watchmaking the next hot career?
bullets.t: Only nine full-time watchmaking schools remain in the US. Rolex runs a tuition-free 18-month program with a $1,800 monthly stipend.

bullets.h: Microbrands' time to shine
bullets.t: Rolex retail prices jumped 18% in two years, while microbrands like Baltic, Serica, and Formex price in the hundreds and low thousands. The microbrand market is expected to grow 25% in five years.

bullets.h: The race to put a doctor on your wrist
bullets.t: Smartwatches have pivoted from step counting to health. Apple added an ECG, then sleep apnea and hypertension alerts. Blood sugar is the next frontier, but no smartwatch can measure it yet. And no federal law stops wearable makers from selling your data.

issues.label: Issue of Jan 19
issues.top: Trump announces new tariffs over Greenland rift

bullets.h: It's MLK Day, the only federal holiday that's also a National Day of Service. US markets were closed.
Trump announces new tariffs over Greenland rift
bullets.t: A 10% tariff on eight European countries is set for Feb. 1, and the EU is weighing up to $108 billion in retaliation.

bullets.h: At least 21 killed in Spain train collision
bullets.t: A high-speed passenger train went off the rails near Córdoba and hit a train coming the other way.

bullets.h: Gaza Board of Peace plan floats $1 billion membership
bullets.t: Member states would serve three-year terms, or pay $1 billion in year one for a permanent seat.

bullets.h: K-food is booming around the world
bullets.t: Korean food exports hit a record $13.6 billion in 2025, and instant noodles jumped nearly 22%.

bullets.h: College football knows how to protect the pocket
bullets.t: Top-division program values are up 46% since last year, and some teams are worth over $1.5 billion. NCAA rule changes allow free transfers and let schools pay athletes up to $20.5 million a year. Indiana's value jumped nearly 68%.

bullets.h: 20%: how much smaller wedding parties are than in 2019
bullets.t: About eight people now versus ten. One writer says seven years of bridesmaid duty cost her nearly $20,000.

bullets.h: Foment
bullets.t: Means 'to promote.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 20
issues.top: Trump says he'll sue JPMorgan over 'debanking'

bullets.h: Matt Damon says Netflix wants a big action scene in the first five minutes and the plot repeated three or four times so doomscrollers don't get lost.
Trump says he'll sue JPMorgan over 'debanking'
bullets.t: He said he'd sue within two weeks. JPMorgan says it doesn't close accounts over political beliefs.

bullets.h: Trump links Greenland push to not winning the Nobel Prize
bullets.t: In a message to Norway's prime minister he said he no longer felt an obligation to think purely of peace.

bullets.h: China's birthrate falls to its lowest since 1949
bullets.t: 5.63 births per 1,000 people, and the population fell for a fourth straight year.

bullets.h: Fashion designer Valentino dies at 93
bullets.t: The Italian designer behind 'Valentino red' launched his house in 1959.

bullets.h: Prince Harry puts the Daily Mail on trial
bullets.t: Harry, Elton John, and Elizabeth Hurley accuse the paper's publisher of unlawful information gathering. The trial runs about nine weeks.

bullets.h: A mini Sphere is headed to Washington
bullets.t: Planned for National Harbor, MD: 6,000 seats, about a third the size of Vegas, at $1 billion or more to build.

bullets.h: 23%: expected jump in data center construction spending this year
bullets.t: Offices, hotels, and warehouses are falling. Data centers would be over 6% of non-residential construction, up from 2% in 2023. The only limit may be finding enough workers.

bullets.h: Fortnight
bullets.t: Means 'a period of two weeks.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 21
issues.top: Investors are officially afraid again

bullets.h: Good news: the sun sets at 5pm in New York tonight, and the next pre-5pm sunset isn't until November.
Investors are officially afraid again
bullets.t: Renewed tariff threats sparked a 'sell America' move. The Dow fell nearly 900 points, and the S&P 500 had its worst day since October.

bullets.h: Trump's Federal Reserve showdown is today
bullets.t: The Supreme Court hears his bid to fire Fed Gov. Lisa Cook. No president has ever removed a Fed governor.

bullets.h: Europe pushes back on Greenland threats
bullets.t: Macron at Davos: 'We prefer respect over bullies.'

bullets.h: Netflix upgrades its Warner Bros. Discovery offer to all cash
bullets.t: The offer is $82.7 billion, and Netflix also reported 325 million subscribers.

bullets.h: The Supreme Court did not rule on Trump's tariffs
bullets.t: No ruling yet. The next possible date is Feb. 20.

bullets.h: Davos can't stop talking about AI
bullets.t: The CEOs of Anthropic and Google DeepMind both expect AI to come for junior-level jobs. Satya Nadella said energy costs will decide the winner of the AI race, and Hassabis put Chinese AI about six months behind the West.

bullets.h: 750: UK chimney sweeps association members, up from about 590 in 2021
bullets.t: Energy prices are pushing Londoners back to wood stoves. Today's sweeps use CCTV instead of little boys.

bullets.h: Dickensian
bullets.t: Relating to living or working conditions below an acceptable standard, like in a Dickens novel.

issues.label: Issue of Jan 22
issues.top: Trump says Greenland deal is coming, tariffs off

bullets.h: The Razzie nominations are out, and the seven artificial dwarfs from Snow White are up for worst supporting actor.
SCOTUS seems poised to let Lisa Cook stay at the Fed
bullets.t: Justices across the spectrum worried that firing her would weaken the central bank's independence.

bullets.h: Jamie Dimon calls Trump's card fee cap an 'economic disaster'
bullets.t: He said a 10% cap would force a drastic reduction in credit cards.

bullets.h: Trump says Greenland deal is coming, tariffs off
bullets.t: He announced a 'framework' with NATO's Mark Rutte and dropped the promised tariffs, and markets rallied.

bullets.h: A massive winter storm is coming
bullets.t: Severe weather is expected to hit more than 200 million Americans across 2,000 miles from Friday.

bullets.h: Curtains come down on Sundance in Utah
bullets.t: After four decades in Park City, the festival moves to Boulder, CO next year. Boulder won with $34 million in tax credits over 10 years.

bullets.h: 11.2 billion: times the NYT's games were played last year
bullets.t: It just launched Crossplay, its first multiplayer game. Subscribers hit 12.33 million.

bullets.h: Dormant
bullets.t: Means 'temporarily inactive.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 23
issues.top: Apple and OpenAI vie for AI gadgets

bullets.h: A huge winter storm is on the way from New Mexico to the East Coast, and airlines are already waiving change fees.
Trump sues JPMorgan and Jamie Dimon over 'debanking'
bullets.t: A $5 billion suit filed in Florida state court. JPMorgan says it has no merit.

bullets.h: Jack Smith testifies publicly about his Trump investigations
bullets.t: He told the House Judiciary Committee 'no one should be above the law.'

bullets.h: Free Solo, but live, comes to Netflix
bullets.t: Alex Honnold plans to climb the 1,667-foot Taipei 101 with no ropes. Weather pushed it back 24 hours.

bullets.h: Apple and OpenAI vie for AI gadgets
bullets.t: Apple may be building an AirTag-sized AI pin with cameras and microphones, possibly out by 2027. OpenAI says it is on track to show its first device in the second half of this year, built with Jony Ive and rumored to be screenless.

bullets.h: A Japanese toilet maker is an AI company now
bullets.t: Toto's stock jumped 11% after Goldman flagged its side business: chipmaking equipment that was 42% of operating income last year.

bullets.h: 16: Oscar nominations for Sinners, a record
bullets.t: It beat the old record of 14. One Battle After Another is still the favorite for best picture.

bullets.h: Harangued
bullets.t: Means 'lectured someone in an aggressive and critical manner.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 24
issues.top: TikTok goes American

bullets.h: It's National Compliment Day. Beware the 'compliminsult,' like being told 'that's actually funny.'
Gold hits a record near $5,000 an ounce
bullets.t: Gold is up 8% on the week and 15% since Jan. 1. Silver topped $100 an ounce for the first time.

bullets.h: Baby, it's cold outside
bullets.t: At least 18 states and DC declared emergencies, and 8,300 flights were canceled for the weekend.

bullets.h: US, Russia, and Ukraine hold first trilateral peace talks
bullets.t: Held in the UAE, they are the first direct Russia-Ukraine talks since the 2022 invasion.

bullets.h: TikTok goes American
bullets.t: A $14 billion deal closed Thursday night. ByteDance keeps 19.9%, and Oracle, Silver Lake, and MGX split 45%. The app won't change much at first, but the new terms collect your precise location.

bullets.h: Former sideline reporter Michele Tafoya is running for Senate in Minnesota
A conspiracy theory says Earth loses gravity for seven seconds on Aug. 12
bullets.t: NASA says it won't.

bullets.h: Three Norwegian ski jumpers were suspended 18 months
bullets.t: They enlarged the crotches of their suits.

bullets.h: A cargo ship spill covered an English beach in raw french fries and onions
Atrocious
bullets.t: Means 'of a very poor quality; extremely bad or unpleasant.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 27
issues.top: Social media is lowkey on trial

bullets.h: It's National Plan a Vacation Day, and research says planning a trip boosts happiness more than taking one.
Gold shatters its $5,000 record as investors seek safety
bullets.t: Gold briefly topped $5,100 and is up more than 80% in 12 months.

bullets.h: Michael Burry says he's buying GameStop
bullets.t: Last week GameStop's CEO bought 500,000 shares for about $21.5 million.

bullets.h: Saudi mega-development Neom will be scaled back
bullets.t: The $1.5 trillion project is being downsized. The Line, a planned self-sustaining city, could become a data center hub.

bullets.h: Social media is lowkey on trial
bullets.t: Jury selection began in Los Angeles in a landmark case accusing Meta, TikTok, and YouTube of causing social media addiction in kids. Snap settled, and 5,000+ similar lawsuits are pending. A WSJ poll found 71% support banning most social media for under-16s.

bullets.h: $3.75: price of the new California Post print edition
bullets.t: Rupert Murdoch's newest tabloid launched with a newsroom of about 80 to 100. Its first front page: 'Oscar Wild.'

bullets.h: Unwieldy
bullets.t: Means 'difficult to manage.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 28
issues.top: EU and India clinch 'the mother of all deals'

bullets.h: A $100 million gift means every US Olympian and Paralympian gets $200,000, so the last-place curler in Milan earns the same as the top hockey scorer.
US consumer confidence falls to its lowest since 2014
bullets.t: The Conference Board's gauge dropped to 84.5, with gas and grocery costs the most-cited worries.

bullets.h: EU and India clinch 'the mother of all deals'
bullets.t: After about 20 years of talks, the deal cuts or removes duties on 90% of the $136 billion in goods traded. India will slash tariffs on European cars from as high as 110% to as low as 10%.

bullets.h: Early issues for TikTok US
bullets.t: In the first five days after the deal closed, app deletions climbed 150%. Users reacted to a new privacy pop-up and reports of blocked videos. TikTok blamed a data center outage, and California's governor announced a probe.

bullets.h: Pinterest lays off 15% of employees to pivot to AI
bullets.t: About 675 of its 4,500 workers are out. AI was cited for nearly 55,000 US layoffs last year.

bullets.h: 85 seconds: the Doomsday Clock's distance from midnight
bullets.t: The closest it has ever been. The Bulletin's chair says AI is supercharging misinformation.

bullets.h: Nigh
bullets.t: Means 'near.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 29
issues.top: Fed holds steady in first rate decision of the year

bullets.h: Southwest has scrapped its 54-year-old open seating policy. Future generations will never know the pain of the back-row middle seat.
Fed holds steady in its first rate decision of the year
bullets.t: Rates stay at 3.5% to 3.75%, the first pause since July after three cuts. Waller and Miran dissented in favor of a cut.

bullets.h: Amazon lays off 16,000 employees
bullets.t: That's 30,000 corporate jobs cut since October, about 10% of its white-collar workforce.

bullets.h: Trump warns Iran its 'time is running out' for a nuclear deal
bullets.t: He said a massive armada is headed toward Iran.

bullets.h: Tesla has its first annual revenue drop
bullets.t: Revenue slipped 3% to $94.8 billion and Q4 profit fell 61%. Tesla plans to invest $2 billion in xAI and stop making the Model S and Model X to build Optimus robots.

bullets.h: Revenue and AI spending grow at Meta and Microsoft
bullets.t: Meta posted record Q4 sales of $59.9 billion and plans up to $135 billion in 2026 capital spending, and its stock rose. Microsoft's capex is up 66%, and its stock fell.

bullets.h: The risky AI assistant clawing its way to viral fame
bullets.t: Moltbot, an open-source assistant built on Claude, is blowing up on GitHub. It runs on your own machine, which leaves you open to prompt injection attacks, so run it on a separate computer.

bullets.h: 4%: Starbucks US same-store sales growth, the first rise since 2023
bullets.t: Revenue rose 5% to $9.9 billion, but profit fell more than 60%.

bullets.h: Forage
bullets.t: Means 'to wander in search of food.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 30
issues.top: Why the value of the US dollar is shedding cents

bullets.h: It's a winter Friday: skip the gym, watch a bad Fast & Furious movie, and Google 'Bahamas wi-fi good?' at 2am.
Why the US dollar is shedding cents
bullets.t: Down 2% this year and almost 11% over the past year. Gold and the Swiss franc are surging at the same time, a sign the dollar may be losing its safe-haven status.

bullets.h: Trump says he'll name his Fed Chair pick today
bullets.t: Former Fed Gov. Kevin Warsh was a 95% favorite on Polymarket.

bullets.h: Melania set to lose a lot of money at the box office
bullets.t: The documentary is expected to earn about $3 million opening weekend against $75 million Amazon spent.

bullets.h: Apple revenue soars on 'staggering' iPhone demand
bullets.t: Revenue grew 16% to about $144 billion, and Tim Cook said 2.5 billion Apple devices are now in use.

bullets.h: Why the market is punishing Microsoft but not Meta
bullets.t: Microsoft fell nearly 10%, erasing $350+ billion, while Meta climbed 10%. Nearly half of Microsoft's contracted future revenue depends on OpenAI.

bullets.h: $10 million: top price for a 30-second Super Bowl ad
bullets.t: The average is $8 million, and nearly 40% of advertisers are new this year.

bullets.h: Beaucoup
bullets.t: French for 'a lot.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 31
issues.top: We have a Fed chair nominee

bullets.h: Sony is making four Beatles movies, one from each band member's perspective, and they won't hit theaters until April 2028.
We have a Fed chair nominee
bullets.t: Trump nominated former Fed Gov. Kevin Warsh to replace Powell. Gold dropped as much as 12% and silver as much as 36% while the dollar soared.

bullets.h: The DOJ released 3+ million pages of Epstein documents
bullets.t: The final release includes more than 3 million pages, 2,000 videos, and 180,000 images.

bullets.h: Actress Catherine O'Hara has died at age 71
bullets.t: Known for Schitt's Creek, Home Alone, and Beetlejuice.

bullets.h: Musk may combine his companies
bullets.t: Reuters says Musk may merge SpaceX with xAI, and Bloomberg says he may merge it with Tesla instead. SpaceX is heading toward a record $50 billion IPO as early as June.

bullets.h: Neil Young gave Greenland residents a year of his music and films
Bryan Johnson picked a fight with the AG1 supplement over its clinical trial
Bridgit Mendler's satellite startup landed a $50 million government contract
Facebook conspiracy theorists claim a 'Leviathan is waking up near Virginia'
bullets.t: The screenshot was doctored.

bullets.h: Terraforming
bullets.t: Means 'transforming a planet so it is suitable for human life.'
